oneOf.description: Shown dashed in the atlas, waiting for the operator's answer.
Activated: the poll carries the producer key and first epoch once.
The operator declined it.

The operator cut this device off: its key no longer opens the door,
and one it never fetched is never handed over. Terminal: stop polling
and stop sending; only a new announcement the operator lets in again
pairs this install anew.
A state this contract version does not know. Keep polling.

AnnouncementStatus.description:
An announcement's state, as its poll reports it. `producer_key` and
`epoch` are present exactly once, on the first poll after activation.

tribe.description:
The tribe the operator placed the producer in when saying yes, on
every poll from then on: the `{tribe}` of each route the key opens.

AnnouncementStatus.title: AnnouncementStatus

BatchId.description: A batch's id: the lowercase hex SHA-256 of its decoded body.

commit_mark.description:
The device's commit mark after this request: a counter of batches Wild
has received (D4a-R).

pending.description:
The states of the device's oldest pending batches, so a device rarely
has to ask (D3).

oneOf.description:
Wild holds the batch durably and will run it through the source's
flow. Drop it from the outbox.

The flow ran it through the sink. Lines Wild did not write as sent are
listed as conflicts. For information only.

Wild held the batch and removed it together with its rows: its
source's retention ended, or the operator erased or retracted them.
Drop it from the outbox and never send it again; a re-send is answered
`expired` and writes nothing.

The door does not know the batch, or a state this contract version
does not know. Keep it; re-send it.

BatchStatus.description: One batch's state, as the status route reports it.
BatchStatus.title: BatchStatus

Conflict.description:
One line of a received batch that the source's flow did not write as
sent.

line.description: The line's number in the batch body, counting from 1.

ConflictCode.description:
What the source's flow did with one line of a received batch instead of
writing it as sent. The other lines are written as sent (D0, D4). Every
code is information: none asks the producer to act or to re-send.

oneOf.description:
A `natural` key already holds other values: the source changed its
own history. The line is not written; Wild counts it on the device
record and shows it in the inbox (D4).

A `position` id already held other bytes — a restored file reached an
offset sent before. Wild wrote the line under a generation it derived
from the line itself (D4).

A `live` id already held other values — a restored copy reused an old
counter. Wild wrote the line under an epoch it derived from the line
itself, and the reply's `new_epoch` directive hands the producer a
fresh epoch for its next records (D4).
A code this contract version does not know.

Directives.description:
What the door tells a device on every reply (D1a): changes it should act
on without a second connection.

new_epoch.description:
Use this epoch for the next `live` records: Wild assigned it after a
collision with a restored copy's counter (D4).

paused.description: The operator paused this producer; keep collecting, send nothing.

rotate_key.description: Rotate to this key; the old one verifies until the overlap ends (D2).

send_interval_secs.description: Send no more often than this many seconds.

vocabulary_changed.description: The vocabulary's ETag changed; fetch it again (D7).

Epoch.description:
A new epoch for a producer's `live` records: a random 128-bit value as 32
lowercase hex digits, never a counter, so a daemon restored from a backup can
never hand out an epoch it issued before (D4a-R).
Epoch.title: Epoch

oneOf.description: Text, at most `max_len` characters.
A number.
`true` or `false`.
An RFC 3339 timestamp, the record's own event time.

The key of a record of another type. A reference keeps the target
type's own key; it is never prefixed with a device.

description.description:
What the field holds, in the operator's words: its meaning, its unit,
an example ("Estimated cost of the session in US dollars, e.g. 0.42").
Wild carries it onto the table's field. Optional; at most 280
characters.

KeyClass.description: How a shape's records get their ids.

oneOf.description:
The id is the shape's declared key fields: a re-read writes nothing
new, and a record changed under its id is refused
(`source_rewrote_history`).

The id is an append-only file's generation and byte offset, in the
reserved fields `_generation` (text) and `_offset` (a whole number); a
restored file's line is re-keyed by Wild (`generation_reassigned`).

The id is a per-install epoch and counter, in the reserved fields
`_epoch` and `_seq` (a whole number), for events seen only in the
moment; never backfilled.

LineCode.description: Why one line was rejected before the batch was received (D1).

oneOf.description: The line is not one JSON object.
The line names no `shape@version`, or one the source does not declare.
A field the shape does not declare.
A field the shape requires is missing.
A field's value is not of the declared kind.
A field's string is longer than its cap.
The line is longer than the line bound.
A code this contract version does not know.

contract_version.description: The contract version it was built against (D1b).

fingerprint.description:
The machine fingerprint: an app-specific HMAC of the machine's stable
identifier. Only a hint for offering continuation, never an identity
(D2).

needs_vocabulary.description: Whether it needs the vocabulary of project and customer names (D7).

references.description:
Existing types of the tribe the producer's shapes reference. It never
writes into them (D4a).

tribe.description: The tribe it proposes, if any. Absent, Wild proposes one (D16).

PairingFile.description:
What a pairing file holds: the door, the pin of its certificate, and the
one-time code. JSON, one object, written owner-only (mode 0600).

door.description:
The door's address: `https://host:port` on the local network or this
computer, `http://host:port` for the kit's own door.

door_certificate.description:
The pin of the door's certificate, `sha256:` and 64 hex digits
([`crate::door_certificate`]). Absent for an `http://` door.

pairing_code.description:
The one-time code that opens the program's announcement: sent once, as
the `wild-pairing-code` header, and never shown or logged.

PairingFile.title: PairingFile

Refusal.description:
A refused request: `4xx`/`5xx` with an ADR-0361 body. Wild keeps nothing
of it.

error.description: A sentence for a human; never decided on.

profile.description: The profile that answered, when the request got that far.

Refusal.title: Refusal

RefusalCode.description:
Why the door refused a whole request. Wild keeps nothing of a refused
request.

oneOf.description:
A line fails its declared shape. The reply lists the rejected lines;
the producer fixes them and re-sends.
A body, a line or a field is over its bound (HTTP 413).

A line names a shape version the source does not declare, or one it
has retired.

The manifest's contract version is not served. `params.supported`
lists the versions that are.

The producer presented a commit mark higher than the daemon's: the
daemon was restored from a backup. `params` is a
[`crate::device::Rewound`]: what it still knows, and how many live
lines of this device it still holds (D4a-R).

The device's received batches not yet processed are over its cap;
keep the batch and retry after `Retry-After` (HTTP 429).

The key does not verify, or opens no route of this request. Every
failure before a key verifies is this one code (HTTP 401).

Wild could not store the batch durably, so it received nothing. Keep
the batch and retry after `Retry-After` (HTTP 503).

The operator paused this device, or its whole producer. Nothing was
received: keep the batch and retry after `Retry-After` (HTTP 503,
[`PAUSED_RETRY_AFTER_SECS`]). The key still opens the door, so the
status route answers, with the `paused` directive, and once the
operator resumes it the same key delivers again: no new pairing, no
new key, no new epoch. A revoked key is `unauthenticated` instead.

No route of the contract answers this method and path (HTTP 404; 405
for a route's path asked with another method). `params` holds the
`method` and `path` asked. Nothing was received: fix the request, as
sending it again unchanged reaches nothing.
A code this contract version does not know.

RejectedLine.description: A line the door rejected before the batch was received (D1).

line.description: The line's number in the body, counting from 1.

known_at.description: When the daemon last received a batch under that mark, RFC 3339.

known_mark.description: The commit mark the daemon still knows.

live_held.description:
The live lines of this device that Wild still holds above
`known_mark`: in receipts it kept, and in the lake. The producer
reports as lost only the live events it counted above `known_mark`
less these.

ShapeDecl.description:
A declared shape: its version, its key class, its fields and the type its
records are proposed to fill.

description.description:
What one record of this shape is, in the operator's words ("One
finished work session in OpenCode"). Optional; at most 280 characters.

key.description:
The fields that form a `natural` key. Empty for a `position` or a
`live` shape, which carry their key parts in reserved fields
([`KeyClass::reserved_parts`]).

target_type.description:
The type the producer proposes this shape fills, usually a new one of
its own. The operator accepts it or maps the shape into another type.

SourceDecl.description: One source a producer feeds: a slug and the shapes it sends.

description.description:
What the source is, in the operator's words ("Usage of the OpenCode
agent on this machine"). Optional; at most 280 characters.

StatusRequest.description: The status route's request: the ids to report on.
StatusRequest.title: StatusRequest

Vocabulary.description: The vocabulary an approved device receives, scoped to its person.
Vocabulary.title: Vocabulary

VocabularyEntry.description:
One entry of the vocabulary: a project's or a customer's key and name. A
title match resolves to the key a reference field carries (D7).

target_type.description: The type the key belongs to, e.g. `Kunde`.

producerKey.description: A producer key, minted when the operator activates the producer (D2).

servers.description: V1: the socket `system/ingest.sock` under the operator's profile, and the daemon's TCP ingest listener when the operator opens one: TLS on loopback and on the local network alike, so a connector takes one road wherever it runs (only an engineer's `WILD_INGEST_BIND` on loopback serves plain). Over TLS the door's certificate is its own, self-signed: the producer pins it by the fingerprint its pairing file carries, `sha256:` and 64 lowercase hex digits of the SHA-256 of the certificate's DER, compares it with the certificate the door shows before it writes a byte, and trusts no CA or name in its place and never sends with the comparison skipped.

x-wild-bounds.description: What one batch may carry. Over a bound the batch is answered 413 `over_bound` and nothing is received. A text field is held to its declared `max_len`.
